title: Online Safety: Children and Young People

speakers.name: Paul Waugh
speakers.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education

contributions.text: 14. What steps she is taking with Cabinet colleagues to help keep children and young people safe online.
contributions.name: Calum Miller

contributions.who: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education (Paul Waugh)
contributions.text: We are working across Government to protect children online and in schools. We are raising the age for accessing social media to 16, restricting livestreaming and contact from unknown adults, and providing practical, evidence-based screen use advice for families. Just last week, we announced measures on removing mobile phones from classrooms—our strongest such restrictions yet. This is all part of our effort to ensure that children get the happy, healthy childhood that they deserve.
contributions.name: Paul Waugh
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education

contributions.text: In the past week, we have rightly focused on the abuse and grooming of young people by powerful men. The sexualisation and sexual abuse of children is always wrong. This morning, I met the Little Feminist Bookclub, an amazing group of girls at the Cooper school in Bicester who are campaigning to ban the use of school uniform in pornographic content. Will the Minister back their campaign, and will he work with colleagues in the Ministry of Justice to identify how that loophole can be closed?
contributions.name: Calum Miller

contributions.text: I pay tribute to the Little Feminist Bookclub for all the work it has done, and to the hon. Gentleman for all his advocacy on its behalf. Just last week, we made it an offence for anyone to pretend to be under the age of 16 for the purpose of pornography, which is an important step in this area. My colleague the Minister for victims and violence against women and girls, who is responsible for this area, has committed to meeting the girls in his constituency, and I look forward to hearing about the outcome of that meeting.
contributions.name: Paul Waugh
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education

contributions.text: I recently visited the Joseph Rowntree school in my constituency for a workshop with Be Internet Citizens on how to give students the important skills needed to spot disinformation. With artificial intelligence making it easier to get disinformation out there, that has to be part of the curriculum. Will the Minister join me in congratulating the Joseph Rowntree school on its work to tackle disinformation?
contributions.name: Mr Luke Charters

contributions.text: Yes, indeed; I congratulate the Joseph Rowntree school on that vital work on misinformation and disinformation. My hon. Friend can rest assured that we will ensure digital and media literacy are at the heart of our curriculum reforms, and that children are indeed protected online.
contributions.name: Paul Waugh
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education

contributions.text: The Conservatives are pleased that the Government have launched a consultation on educational technology. The Department for Education acknowledges the harm that ed tech can expose children to, including harm to their social, mental and emotional health. However, I am particularly concerned about the wild west of AI chatbots. When it came to the mobile phone ban in schools, the Government spent a lot of time dithering and delaying; they rejected a ban in seven votes, but then they finally caught up with us Conservatives. The consultation is ongoing, but in the meantime, what will the Minister do about potential harm from the use of AI chatbots in our schools?
contributions.name: Saqib Bhatti

contributions.text: AI chatbots are not in our schools. Our guidance is very clear that they should not be used in schools. Although the hon. Gentleman talks about inaction, it was his Government who failed to act in this crucial area. Our ed tech test beds are gathering the evidence, and are ensuring that teachers are in the driving seat, and that anything we do in schools is guided by the safety and efficacy of the technology.
contributions.name: Paul Waugh
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education
